item.description:
Two more rings, a third thing right-click can do, trackpad gestures that take

modifiers — and, from this version on, MiddleRing updates itself.

Quick access ring

A fixed list of apps in the order you put them in. The switcher is ordered by

recency, which is the right answer for switching and the wrong one for muscle

memory; this ring never moves, so the direction is learnable.

A pinned app that is closed keeps its slot, shows a dimmed icon, and launches

when you commit it. One that has been uninstalled leaves the ring rather than

sitting there failing.

App shortcut ring

Keystrokes for whichever app is in front, under names you gave them. Open it in

Figma and you get Figma's; open it in a browser and you get the browser's.

Committing a slot posts that keystroke straight to the app.

A slot shows the keystroke by default — using the ring is how you stop needing

it — or a symbol picked from a short grid of SF Symbols and emoji, which is

quicker to pick out of a circle at speed. A "global" set sits under whatever the

frontmost app contributes, so the ring is not empty in an app you have not got

round to configuring.

Solo

Right-click a slot to minimize everything that does not belong to that app and

switch to it. App-level even when you aimed at a single window: "leave me with

this one" means the app you are about to work in.

A second solo on the same app restores exactly what the first one minimized —

not everything currently minimized, which would also undo whatever you had

tidied away yourself.

Trackpad gestures take modifiers

Kept separate from a ring's keyboard and mouse modifiers, so binding a ring to

⌃⌥⌘L does not silently demand ⌃⌥⌘ on its finger gesture too.

That also makes two fingers bindable. On its own it is the system's secondary

click and taking that from every app is not a setting anyone would look for

again; under ⌃ or ⌥ it is a gesture nothing else claims.

It updates itself now

The hard part of updating was never noticing that a new version exists — it is

replacing a running app in place with its Developer ID signature intact, and

getting that wrong costs you the Accessibility grant along with the app. So this

uses Sparkle, and the update feed is signed with a key whose private half never

leaves the developer's machine.

This is the last version you have to install by hand. 0.2.0 shipped without

an updater, so it cannot pull this one down; from 0.3.0 onward MiddleRing checks

for itself and offers the update in place. There is a "Check for updates" item in

the menu bar and a switch in Settings › Genel if you would rather it did not.

Also

  • Rings are a list internally rather than two hand-copied blocks of settings, so

the next one costs an enum case. Triggers you had already chosen are migrated;

nothing needs re-binding.

  • Fixed: nested Sparkle components failed notarization on the first attempt,

which is worth saying out loud because codesign --deep --strict passes on

exactly that mistake.

Requirements

macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon. MiddleRing needs Accessibility permission —

that is what lets it read the window list and bring a window forward. Screen

Recording is only requested if you turn live previews on.

Install

Open the DMG, drag MiddleRing to Applications, launch it, and grant

Accessibility when asked. It lives in the menu bar; there is no Dock icon.

Signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple, so it opens

without a Gatekeeper warning.
